promise: End the Russia-Ukraine war within 24 hours of becoming president
description: Trump promised repeatedly, including at a January 7, 2025 press conference, that he would have the war 'solved within 24 hours' of returning to office. The war continued throughout 2025 and remained active in 2026.
evidence: No ceasefire or peace deal within 24 hours of inauguration

promise: "When I win, I will immediately bring prices down, starting on Day One."
description: At an August 2024 campaign press conference surrounded by groceries, Trump pledged to bring prices down immediately, starting on Day One of his presidency. Instead, consumer prices and egg prices rose through January 2025, and Democratic lawmakers wrote that his price-related promises had gone unfulfilled.
evidence: No Day One price drop; food and egg prices rose in January 2025
Democratic lawmakers' January 2025 letter cited unfulfilled price promises

promise: "If the hostages are not released prior to January 20, 2025, there will be all hell to pay."
description: In December 2024 Trump warned there would be 'all hell to pay' if Hamas did not release hostages before his January 20, 2025 inauguration. Not all hostages were freed by that date, but his pressure contributed to the ceasefire deal announced January 19, under which hostages were released in phases through the following months.
evidence: Not all hostages were released by January 20, 2025
Ceasefire deal led to phased releases starting January 19, 2025; Trump credited his envoy with the deal
